products.name: Devin (Cognition)
products.note: Autonomous software engineer; full codebase access; high decision-influence; security critical

reading.body:
Cognition operates two products with direct access to production code and decision-making authority in software engineering workflows, creating security-critical dependencies on AI system reliability.

Devin, an autonomous software engineer with full codebase access, and Windsurf, an AI IDE with source-code visibility, represent a shift in how enterprises deploy AI into their development pipelines. These are not recommendation engines or assistants that humans filter before acting. They write, test, and ship code with minimal human intervention by design. This concentrates the attack surface and failure modes of downstream systems into the reliability and security posture of a single vendor's models and infrastructure.

The company's 181 recorded litigation cases in California flag operational or contractual friction. This does not indicate whether cases involve product liability, employment, IP disputes, or regulatory matters, but the volume suggests friction points worth examining for companies considering integration into critical workflows.

The data does not reveal Cognition's compute footprint, power consumption, or infrastructure dependencies. It does not show whether Devin and Windsurf run on proprietary hardware, cloud platforms, or customer premises, or what redundancy and governance structures protect production systems that delegate code decisions to these tools. These gaps matter because autonomous decision-making in code deployment amplifies the downstream consequences of any infrastructure failure.

profile_text.body:
Cognition is a for-profit startup founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. On its website the company describes itself as the operator of Devin, which it calls the first autonomous software engineer. According to the site, Devin plans, writes, tests, and ships production code inside a customer's existing workflows. The company also publishes FrontierCode, a benchmark it describes as measuring whether a model writes code that a maintainer would actually merge, combining custom rubrics, novel verifiers, and tests to check correctness, test quality, scope discipline, style, and adherence to codebase standards. Cognition describes itself as a team of interdisciplinary makers working on the hardest problems in AI and as supporting leading enterprises and technology companies.

Two products are tracked for the company. Devin (Cognition) is listed as an autonomous software engineer with full codebase access and high decision-influence, and Windsurf is listed as an AI IDE with source-code exposure. The company's litigation exposure is recorded in California, with a count of 281, and no individual cases are listed. No MCP servers are recorded for it.
